reuse.why: A single guardBankAccountLink wrapper covers every provider and Fintegra reuses the SimpleFin linker, but the takeover step re-writes unlinkAccount's field reset inline and Fintegra's download copies the Akahu/Pluggy downloader instead of sharing it.

duplication.why: Adds a copy of the unlink db.updateAccount block and a third copy of the token-post-transactions download; the new finishBankAccountLink tail is applied to some linkers but not Akahu, which keeps its own copy.

placement.why: The link rules sit in one wrapper at handler registration in accounts/app.ts and the download in accounts/sync.ts, as the tree does for other providers; making linkSimpleFinAccount serve Fintegra puts a different provider's rules inside a provider-named function.

scope.why: Changes stay on linking and Fintegra; extracting the sync-and-notify tail is a small refactor beyond the request, done for only some linkers.

maintainability.why: The guard is easy to own, but copied unlink logic can drift from unlinkAccount, and 'SimpleFin linker with a provider flag plus an orgDomain-in check' is a fragile way to add a provider.

bypasses_abstraction.where: app.ts guardBankAccountLink clears the old link with its own db.updateAccount instead of unlinkAccount (or an extracted reset shared with it); sync.ts downloadFintegraTransactions re-implements the provider download.

disguised_duplication.where: The unlink reset is a verbatim copy and the Fintegra downloader a lightly condensed copy of Akahu's; neither is meaningfully disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: linkSimpleFinAccount gains a provider parameter and an 'orgDomain' in externalAccount special case to serve Fintegra; guardBankAccountLink's inline unlink bypasses unlinkAccount and downloadFintegraTransactions re-implements the shared download shape (linkAkahuAccount also skips finishBankAccountLink).
